basis: Branch Tarawa assault begins 24 Nov under favorable observed-depth/high-water plan; later LCVP/LCM use is materially earlier than historical 20 Nov reef-wading case.
Current Branch D-Day ledger already fixes first 87 LVT destroyed-or-mission-killed at 14-19 and an additional 18-26 damaged, many locally repairable.
Historical sanity anchor: 125 LVT committed; only 35 operational at battle end, with 90 out/lost. Historical attrition is not copied because Branch exposure geometry and shuttle demand differ.

December_recovery_gate.note: This does not transfer these vehicles into FLINTLOCK/CATCHPOLE by fiat. Unit ownership, refit and shipping remain separate gates.

why_branch_is_better_than_historical: Verified channels and rising tide reduce prolonged exposed reef shuttle work.
LCVP/LCM assume a larger share of later-day supply movement.
Many D-Day damage cases are mission-kill/repairable rather than deep-water disappearance.
US recovery/maintenance learns rapidly during a longer battle.
why_not_near_zero_losses: Japanese surviving direct fire is denser than the old branch line.
LVTs still make repeated exposed movements on D-Day and early D+1.
Coral, salt water, mechanical wear and enemy fire continue after the beachhead is formed.
